Unfortunately, what should have been the benchmark for future legislation surrounding the right to vote is no more. We’ve seen an unprecedented amount of attacks on the right to vote in recent years.

State legislatures across the country have introduced some of the most restrictive pieces of legislation to make it more difficult for everyday people to participate in elections.

Hi Peter, it’s Tammy Baldwin.

Last night, the Republican presidential candidates descended on Milwaukee for their first nationally-televised debate. Wisconsin is the premier battleground state in this critical election, and the GOP is laser-focused on putting every possible resource into flipping our state — and my Senate seat — red. Let me explain:

Wisconsin’s 10 electoral votes were the tipping point in the last two presidential elections. Our state put Joe Biden over the top in 2020 and tipped the presidency to Donald Trump in 2016.

**Both elections were decided by less than 1% — that’s about 20,000 votes.**

Last year’s Senate race in Wisconsin was also decided by a razor-thin margin. Republicans won by 1% after spending a record $77 million to defend GOP Sen. Ron Johnson.

If we can win those 20,000 votes, the White House and the Senate majority are virtually guaranteed to stay in Democratic hands. But if we lose those critical votes next November, Republicans will have their best shot at flipping both. Those are the stakes in Wisconsin.

Election experts are already calling us “the tipping point state,” “the most pivotal of all the battlegrounds,” “a potential decider,” “the indispensable state,” and “the most fiercely contested partisan battleground in the nation.”

With Wisconsin’s 10 electoral votes in play again and the Senate majority up for grabs, national Republicans are going all-in to win in our state — starting with the first GOP debate and the Republican National Convention next summer.

The GOP will throw everything they have into defeating me and flipping Wisconsin red, and I’m fighting back as hard as I possibly can. But I cannot do it alone.

body:
Happy Labor Day, Peter!

Today, we honor the workers who organized to improve working conditions for people across the country. From the 40-hour work week to minimum wage and safer working conditions to the creation of Social Security and implementation of child labor laws, we have a lot to thank the labor movement for.

I know that the path to a strong middle class starts with empowering workers and building unions. That's why I'll always stand with workers across Missouri who are organizing to fight for better wages and working conditions.

It’s time Missourians had a senator who will fight for every worker’s right to organize.

Unlike Josh Hawley, I know that Missouri’s workers are the backbone of our state. Workers are coming together to demand dignity and respect at every level across our state at this moment. It’s not just happening in factories or construction sites, but in law offices, fast food restaurants, hospitals, and local coffee shops.

Every worker deserves jobs with dignity and respect. In the Senate, I’ll fight to pass legislation that ensures workplaces are paying workers fairly, providing benefits like quality health insurance, and creating safer working conditions.

Today, please join me in honoring the accomplishments of the workers who came before us.

Have a safe and happy Labor Day,

Wesley

Happy Veterans Day, Peter.

Today, we take the time to honor the bravery and selflessness of the many service members who risked their lives to defend our nation.

More than 355,000 veterans live in Missouri, and nearly 34,000 of them call Missouri's 1st district home. These veterans live amongst us as our friends, family, and neighbors who have made incredible sacrifices to keep us safe and protect our democracy, and for that, we'll be forever indebted to them.

This Veterans Day, we remember those who put everything on the line to serve our country. Because the challenges veterans face don't end when their service does, we must commit to honoring and supporting our veterans as they continue to return home and their families.

My message to all veterans in Missouri and across the country is this: **Thank you for your service, sacrifice, and commitment to protecting our country.**

Thank you,

Wesley Bell

body:
It was never going to stop with Roe v. Wade The “Alliance Defending Freedom” (ADF) right-wing special interest group, notorious for its role in overturning _Roe v. Wade,_ is once again at the forefront of another alarming anti-freedom, anti-choice effort.

**This time, they are challenging the FDA's regulation over mifepristone, a safe and widely-used abortion pill. And soon, the Supreme Court will decide whether or not they’ll protect access to this life-saving medication.**

The ADF is trying to use an outdated 19th-century law to bypass medical expertise and restrict access to crucial healthcare services, including medication abortions._But I want to be clear about something:_ **This isn't just about FDA regulations; it's a calculated attack on reproductive rights across the nation.**

Personal decisions about reproductive health should be made between individuals and their doctors, not dictated by a vocal minority of extremists. When elected to Congress, I’ll remain a proud pro-choice leader and a strong voice for the majority of Americans, _which includes most St. Louisans_ , who understand that reproductive care IS healthcare.

When elected to Congress, I’ll ALWAYS vote to protect reproductive freedom. But if we’re going to build a winning campaign and take back the House majority in November, we’ll need all hands on deck. body:
I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class. Peter — I am proud to come from a union family.

I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class, _that’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by six labor unions in St. Louis._

Building a stronger economy starts with fortifying workers' rights and ensuring equity for working Americans. As a former union member (NEA), I understand the importance of standing shoulder-to-shoulder with workers.

In 1967, my grandfather, Reverend Melvin T. Bell, fearlessly spearheaded a strike against Duncan Foundry and Machine Works in Alton, Ill. His leadership resulted in significant improvements in pay and benefits for workers, culminating in a landmark ruling by the National Labor Relations Board.

Fast forward to 2018, amidst the fight against "right-to-work" laws, I took to the streets, knocking on doors to rally support to defeat Proposition A. Together, we stood firm urging voters to say "NO" to measures that threatened workers' rights and fair labor practices. **In Washington, D.C., I will continue to be a strong advocate for workers' rights and a voice that amplifies the need for fair wages and equitable treatment.**

President Joe Biden is making strides at providing good-paying jobs across the nation, and I am committed to advancing these initiatives rather than hindering them. But if I’m going to cross the finish line this November, I’m going to need the support of this grassroots team.

body:
I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class. Peter — I am proud to come from a union family.

I know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class, _that’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by six labor unions in St. Louis._

Building a stronger economy starts with fortifying workers' rights and ensuring equity for working Americans. As a former union member (NEA), I understand the importance of standing shoulder-to-shoulder with workers.

In 1967, my grandfather, Reverend Melvin T. Bell, fearlessly spearheaded a strike against Duncan Foundry and Machine Works in Alton, Ill. His leadership resulted in significant improvements in pay and benefits for workers, culminating in a landmark ruling by the National Labor Relations Board.

Fast forward to 2018, amidst the fight against "right-to-work" laws, I took to the streets, knocking on doors to rally support to defeat Proposition A. Together, we stood firm urging voters to say "NO" to measures that threatened workers' rights and fair labor practices. **In Washington, D.C., I will continue to be a strong advocate for workers' rights and a voice that amplifies the need for fair wages and equitable treatment.**

President Joe Biden is making strides at providing good-paying jobs across the nation, and I am committed to advancing these initiatives rather than hindering them. But if I’m going to cross the finish line this November, I’m going to need the support of this grassroots team.

subject: Ensuring a brighter tomorrow for future generations
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter,

We must come to grips with the reality that we will continue to feel the effects of climate change across all sectors of our life.

In Missouri, we're already feeling the impacts of climate change on our way of life and the safety of vulnerable communities. That’s why I've made it a priority on this campaign to engage with advocacy groups to better understand the challenges our St. Louis faces.

body:
**Happy Teacher Appreciation Week, Peter!**

I want to express my deepest gratitude to all educators, _especially those right here in St. Louis._

Our teachers tirelessly dedicate themselves both inside and outside the classroom to shaping the minds and futures of our nation's youth, despite the never-ending obstacles thrown their way.

Extreme legislators in Congress are seemingly hell-bent on undermining and attacking our teachers and education system, cutting funding, and pushing archaic book bans.

America’s teachers are consistently undervalued, underpaid, and overworked. And relentless attacks from groups like Moms for Liberty, are actively making their jobs harder with their dangerous agenda. _But let me make one thing clear:_ **As someone who believes in the value of education, Missouri's families and their students deserve better.**

Our educators deserve to be paid a livable wage, and our students deserve an education rooted in facts, free of extremist political interference.

That’s why, in Congress, I’ll always fight to ensure our children have access to a quality education that will help them succeed.

I'll never stop fighting to make investments that support our public schools right here in St. Louis, and across our state. body:
Extreme Republicans have used voter suppression tactics to silence the voices of millions. There is nothing more fundamental to defending our democracy than protecting our voting rights.

But, Peter, that hasn’t stopped extreme Republicans from using voter suppression tactics and silencing the voices of millions – _particularly in marginalized communities_ – to try and advance their own agenda.

Including shamelessly stalling the _John Lewis Voting Rights Act_ , a critical piece of legislation designed to protect and expand the right to vote for every American. _**But that’s not all, they’ve also...**_
* **Enacted stricter voter ID laws:** Implementing stringent ID requirements that disproportionately affect minorities, the elderly, and low-income voters.
* **Purged voter rolls:** Removing millions of voters from registration lists, often without proper notification, targeting communities of color and young voters.
* **Attempting to reduce early voting:** Cutting back on early voting days and hours, making it harder for people with inflexible schedules to vote.
* **Closing Polling Places:** Shutting down polling locations in predominantly minority and low-income neighborhoods, leading to longer lines and wait times.
* **Gerrymandering their way to victory:** Drawing district lines to dilute the voting power of specific communities, ensuring Republican majorities despite popular vote totals.

[**Peter, will you consider chipping in just $10, $5, or whatever you can to help me fight back by building a winning campaign ahead of November? >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/85384837/474581510/1027042714?refcode=em24_240521_votefr_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em24_240521_votefr_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=5c66803f-c017-ef11-86d0-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNWM2NjgwM2YtYzAxNy1lZjExLTg2ZDAtNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=15lbRfRdWn1mtKLhn5BXsklYIoZ84lIFHmLtxiKizcg=)

subject: Celebrating the fallen, and honoring the promises made to those who are still with us.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Memorial Day is not just a day off but a time to reflect on the true cost of freedom. It’s a day to pay tribute to our fallen heroes and express our gratitude for their service – _**their courage and dedication has secured many of the freedoms we cherish today.**_

As we gather with family and friends this Memorial Day, let us take a moment to remember and honor the brave men and women who have made the ultimate sacrifice for our country.

In Congress, I’ll always vote to support the families they left behind and stand with the veterans who are still with us, _who have given so much._ Their service and sacrifice should never be forgotten. Today, and everyday, I hope you’ll join me in honoring our heroes.

**Wishing you a safe and peaceful Memorial Day.**

Thank you,

Wesley

Peter – in a moment, I'm going to ask you to consider [**chipping in $5, or whatever you can, to help me build a winning campaign.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86051973/476686918/1027042714?refcode=em24_240531_EOM5_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em24_240531_EOM5_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=a5f955ab-ae1f-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTVmOTU1YWItYWUxZi1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=jG7nOAXT1uW8IhKRia6bbWFLDgLOd-PKs_pPsnv9ljM=) _But first, I want to tell you a bit about this campaign and what your support means to me:_

I’ve proudly dedicated my career working to find real solutions for everyday folks all across our district.

As the proud son of a police officer and county civil servant, public service has always been in my DNA. And in 2018, I was elected as Missouri's first African-American top prosecutor. It was a tough fight, but with you by my side, **we made history.**

Together, we’ve taken a strong stand against violent criminals while empowering our community. I've worked with the Department of Justice to reform Ferguson's criminal justice system, improved police training, introduced body cams, raised police pay, and overhauled the court system. I’ve also created the North County Police Cooperative – a community-policing model – and expanded diversion programs with a nearly _90% success_ rate.

But Peter, beyond this, if you take anything away from this email, _here’s what I want you to know:_ My drive to fight for St. Louisans has only grown since launching this people-powered campaign. I’m committed to strengthening our economy, lowering health costs, reinvesting in rural areas, protecting reproductive freedom, supporting seniors, and fighting climate change. body:
The freedom to love and the fight ahead: Happy Pride Month, Peter!

**This month, we honor the LGBTQ+ community, celebrating their strength, resilience, and the vibrant diversity they bring to our communities and our world.** But, as we celebrate, it's important to remember the ongoing challenges LGBTQ+ folks face, especially right here in Missouri.

Across the country, we've seen a rise in anti-LGBTQ+ laws that threaten the rights and safety of our friends, neighbors, and family members. The ACLU is tracking 39 different bills in our state legislature alone that are attempting to take away the rights of LGBTQ+ folks.

These laws are not just words on paper; they represent a dangerous step backward, putting the safety and dignity of LGBTQ+ individuals at risk every single day.

From restrictions on gender-affirming care to bans on discussing sexual orientation and gender in schools, these measures aim to erase the identities and experiences of many Missourians, including those in St. Louis.

**While we've made progress in protecting the rights of all Americans, our work is far from over. Discrimination and prejudice still exist, and we must continue to fight for equality and justice for ALL Americans.**

I hope you'll join me in supporting the LGBTQ+ community and their allies – not just in June, _**but every single day.**_ Together, we can create a society where everyone is treated with dignity, respect, and equality, _no matter who they love or how they identify._

Wishing you a happy and safe Pride Month!

In solidarity,

body:
The journey towards gender equality is far from over, especially here in Missouri. Peter,

The Equal Pay Act of 1963 was a groundbreaking decision that aimed to ensure men and women receive equal pay for equal work. While this was a crucial step forward for gender equity – _our journey is far from complete._

Sadly, Missouri ranks **12th** in the country for having the widest gender pay gap. **Women in Missouri earn an average of $45,034 annually, which is 20.9% less than the $56,983 earned by men.** This means women are earning just 79 cents for every dollar that white men earn, a gap that is even larger for women of color, who face even more severe disparities simply for the color of their skin.

These numbers represent more than just statistics. They reflect real struggles and lost opportunities for women and families throughout Missouri. The gender pay gap means less money for essentials like housing, education, and healthcare, and it perpetuates economic insecurity for countless women, and their families, all across our state.

But Peter, gender equality is more than a principle; it’s a necessity. Equal pay for equal work is a fundamental right, and we must continue pushing for policies that reflect the core values of our democracy, starting with electing leaders like Wesley Bell, who will always stand up for every-day people.

Wesley is committed to closing the gender pay gap in Congress, and will always vote to ensure that women in Missouri – _including thousands here in St. Louis_ – are afforded the same opportunities, respect, and pay as their white, male counterparts.

clean_body: The journey towards gender equality is far from over, especially here in Missouri. Peter, The Equal Pay Act of 1963 was a groundbreaking decision that aimed to ensure men and women receive equal pay for equal work. While this was a crucial step forward for gender equity – our journey is far from complete. Sadly, Missouri ranks 12th in the country for having the widest gender pay gap. Women in Missouri earn an average of $45,034 annually, which is 20.9% less than the $56,983 earned by men. This means women are earning just 79 cents for every dollar that white men earn, a gap that is even larger for women of color, who face even more severe disparities simply for the color of their skin. These numbers represent more than just statistics. They reflect real struggles and lost opportunities for women and families throughout Missouri. The gender pay gap means less money for essentials like housing, education, and healthcare, and it perpetuates economic insecurity for countless women, and their families, all across our state. But Peter, gender equality is more than a principle; it’s a necessity. Equal pay for equal work is a fundamental right, and we must continue pushing for policies that reflect the core values of our democracy, starting with electing leaders like Wesley Bell, who will always stand up for every-day people. Wesley is committed to closing the gender pay gap in Congress, and will always vote to ensure that women in Missouri – including thousands here in St. Louis – are afforded the same opportunities, respect, and pay as their white, male counterparts. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- = | | = | | = ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you, Jordan Sanders Campaign Manager Team Bell = = PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI 7253 WATSON RD #1115, ST LOUIS, MO 63119

_“The ruling is a significant setback for the anti-abortion movement in what was the first major Supreme Court case on reproductive rights since the court’s conservative majority overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022.”_ Peter,

In a unanimous 9-0 decision, the Supreme Court ruled to uphold access to mifepristone, the medication commonly used in medication abortions.

Today’s ruling is a crucial win for the majority of Americans who believe in the right to choose and the necessity of safe and legal abortion care. It is a testament to our ongoing fight for reproductive justice, and the tireless work of advocates across the country.

But Peter, while we celebrate this victory, we can’t forget that this is the same Supreme Court that overturned _Roe v. Wade_ , striking down decades of settled law that protected a woman's right to choose. **The fight for reproductive rights is far from over. We can expect the challenges to women’s autonomy over their bodies from extremist, anti-choice justices and politicians to continue.**

In Congress, I will ALWAYS stand with the pro-choice majority of Americans – and St. Louisans – who believe that healthcare decisions should be left between a person and their doctor, including the right to have an abortion. **I am committed to defending and expanding reproductive freedom,** and will fight against any attempts to roll back our rights in the House.

Thank you for your ongoing support.

In solidarity,

More than two years after president Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation: **Happy Juneteenth, Peter!**

On this day in 1865, Union soldiers arrived in Galveston, Texas, to announce the end of the Civil War and the freedom of all enslaved people – _more than two years after President Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation._

Juneteenth serves as a powerful testament to the progress we’ve made in the fight for liberation and equality – **but it is also a stark reminder for all of us that there is still much more we must do to realize the promise of a country where people are _truly_ equal. **

This year, let us come together as a community to honor the resilience and contributions of Black Americans throughout history. Whether through local events, conversations with loved ones, or personal reflection, **I hope you’ll join me in observing Juneteenth and reaffirm your commitment to building a more inclusive and just nation for ALL.**

body:
Peter,

As we celebrate Pride Month, I am reminded of the power, beauty, and diversity of our LQBTQ+ communities both in St. Louis and nationwide.

Pride is a time to honor and celebrate the progress made by and for the LGBTQ+ communities and the courage it takes for LGBTQ+ individuals to live openly and authentically.

But, this month, beyond the celebrations – **I can’t help but to also think about the challenges many LGBTQ+ folks still face, especially here in Missouri**. In recent months and years, we've seen a wave of dangerous and discriminatory anti-LGBTQ+ legislation introduced by extreme legislators.

These laws aim to undermine the rights and freedoms of our LGBTQ+ friends, family members, and neighbors. They target everything from healthcare access to the ability to express one’s identity openly. This trend is not only deeply troubling, but it also threatens the fundamental principles of equality and justice that we should all stand for.

These legislative attacks are a stark reminder of the work that still lies ahead. But Peter, the majority of Americans – _which includes most St. Louisans_ – believe in a world where everyone should be allowed to live openly and freely, without fearing for their lives and safety. It's about more than just policies; it's about ensuring that every person, regardless of who they are or who they love, can lead a life filled with dignity, respect, and happiness.

We must come together to challenge these extreme lawmakers and advocate for policies that protect and uplift the LGBTQ+ community. **This means supporting inclusive education, protecting healthcare rights, and ensuring that anti-discrimination laws are not only upheld but strengthened.** So, as we celebrate Pride this month, let's also recommit to the fight for equality.

**Simply put: There is no place for hate or discrimination in our state OR country.**

In solidarity,

Peter,

The Fourth of July is a time to come together with family, friends, and community. It's a day to enjoy good food, great company, and, of course, some spectacular fireworks.

**But beyond all else, it's a reminder of the incredible journey our nation has taken since 1776, and the promise of freedom and equality that we're all striving to achieve.**

As we celebrate, it's important that we also recognize that our work for justice and equality is ongoing. To build a more perfect union and truly live up to the ideals of freedom and equality for all, we must stay vigilant, engaged, and active.

Over the last few years and months, it's been made clear that our fundamentals are only guaranteed when we come together to defend them. So, while you and your loved ones enjoy your celebrations, let's keep working towards a brighter and more just future for every American – _**because none of us are truly free until ALL of us are.**_

Wishing you and your loved ones a happy and safe Independence Day!

We’re days away from our August 6 primary. That’s why I’m reaching out: Peter,

In just a moment, [**I'm going to ask you to chip in $5, or whatever you can, to help us build a winning campaign ahead of our August 6 primary.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90045517/489243311/1027045913?refcode=em24_240801_fp1_fndd_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_campaign=em24_240801_fp1_fndd_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=dc6efc72-5550-ef11-86c3-6045bdee6681&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGM2ZWZjNzItNTU1MC1lZjExLTg2YzMtNjA0NWJkZWU2NjgxIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZxSw1SwKnpDBKvm76pp2u9B69VT942V2PTITFIoDppY=)

But first, _I want to share why this final push ahead of primary day is so crucial._

Born and raised in North St. Louis County, the proud son of a police officer and county civil servant, public service is not just a career for me – **it's fundamental to who I am.**

More than ever before, we need legislators who will fight for the people they were elected to represent, not the deep-pocketed special interests or their own personal interests. We need leaders in Congress who will work across party lines and ensure they’re in lockstep with their own constituents and fellow Democratic legislators.

But right now, that’s just not the way things are. Congress is a huge mess. House leadership – _on both sides of the aisle_ – is more divided than ever. **And instead of addressing the real issues facing our nation, we’ve got House Republicans who are busy playing politics, and ready to do whatever it takes to push a dangerous MAGA agenda – even if it’s at the expense of their own communities.**

I’ve spent my life working to find real solutions to the challenges faced by everyday Missourians. Since I was elected as Missouri's first African-American top prosecutor for our largest prosecuting attorney's office, I have been dedicated to tackling the issues that real folks care about. And in Congress, I will do everything I possibly can to ensure that we’re passing laws that benefit St. Louisans – _and all Americans_ – directly.

I am proud of the work we've done together, but my drive to do more for the people of Missouri has only gotten stronger. I know my work, and journey, in public service is far from over. I will always fight tooth and nail for the things that matter most to YOU. From protecting reproductive freedom for all to taking on special interests to get weapons of war off of our streets to fighting to protect our environment and expand crucial programs like Social Security and Medicare – _I will always fight for your needs._

**But, Peter, I won’t be able to cross the finish line on primary day without your help.**

[**Can I count on you to chip in $5, or anything you can, so that we can continue to build this grassroots campaign in these final days before our August 6 primary? Your support will help me reach more voters, share our vision for a better future, and ensure that our community's voice is heard in Washington. >>**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/90045518/489243312/1027045913?refcode=em24_240801_fp1_fndd_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_campaign=em24_240801_fp1_fndd_gq_act___wb_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=dc6efc72-5550-ef11-86c3-6045bdee6681&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGM2ZWZjNzItNTU1MC1lZjExLTg2YzMtNjA0NWJkZWU2NjgxIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=ZxSw1SwKnpDBKvm76pp2u9B69VT942V2PTITFIoDppY=)

Thank you for all you have done and continue to do for me and this campaign.

Onward to victory,

subject: The right to vote is part of the American promise.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter – our democracy is under threat.

Across the country, extremist politicians are passing laws that make it harder for everyday Americans – _including St. Louisans_ – to vote, spreading dangerous lies that threaten the very cornerstones of our democracy.

subject: My gratitude for America’s laborers is personal.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter,

As we celebrate Labor Day, **I want to take a moment to express my heartfelt appreciation for the hard-working Americans who are the backbone of this nation.**

I am proud to come from a union family and know firsthand the crucial role unions play for workers and the working class. That’s why I was beyond honored to have been endorsed by six labor unions in St. Louis.

Building a stronger economy starts with fortifying workers’ rights and ensuring equity for working Americans. As a former union member (NEA), I understand the importance of standing shoulder-to-shoulder with workers.

I am beyond ready to take this ongoing fight to the halls of Congress, where I will continue to be a strong advocate for workers’ rights and a voice that amplifies the need for fair wages and equitable treatment.

**So today – _and every day_ – I hope you’ll join me in honoring the contributions of laborers from all walks of life and recommit to protecting and expanding workers’ rights for EVERY American.**

Wishing you a safe and restful Labor Day,

Onward,

Wesley

_“Both sides of the debate over whether to enshrine abortion rights in Missouri’s constitution have filed last-minute legal challenges hoping to influence how, and if, the proposal goes before voters.”_ Peter,

Right now, anti-abortion extremists are pulling out all the stops to block progress for women across Missouri.

They’re doing everything in their power to defy Missouri’s pro-choice majority from securing the right to reproductive freedom in our state constitution.

As a proud pro-choice candidate, _I’ve always believed that a woman’s right to make her own healthcare decisions is non-negotiable._ This isn’t just about politics — it’s about ensuring every woman in Missouri has the freedom to control her own body, her own life, and her own future.

Peter, let me be clear: **Abortion care is health care, plain and simple**. And without it, countless Missouri women could be left without the essential care they need, putting their lives at risk in more ways than one. In Congress, I will always fight for every woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions, _free from government or extremist interference._

body:
Our numbers are about to go public. Peter,

Now that we’re *officially* on the ballot for November’s election, it’s now full steam ahead until Election Day.

I’m proud to stand by my progressive record as a judge, city council member, and as the St. Louis County Prosecuting Attorney. I’ve worked tirelessly to put St. Louisans first, delivering real results and fighting for the people. **I can’t wait to get to Congress to keep fighting for your best interests at every level.**

St. Louisans have made it clear they’re ready to elect a for-the-people leader to represent them in Congress – someone who will really listen to their voice and make their concerns the priority. I’m so thankful for this grassroots team, for everything you’ve done to get us this far. But we can’t get complacent.

Now, we’re coming up against a critical FEC end-of-quarter deadline, and my team and I have set an ambitious $20,500 fundraising goal to keep our momentum going. body:
Peter,

This MLK Day, we honor the life and legacy of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., a leader who taught us that progress is possible when we stand together for justice, equality, and the dignity of every human being.

Dr. King’s dream wasn’t just about hope – it was about action. He challenged systems of oppression, marched in the face of danger, and spoke truth to power even when the stakes were high. As we reflect on his legacy, _let’s remember that the work isn’t over._

Today, the fight for voting rights, economic justice, and racial equality continues – and it’s up to us to carry Dr. King’s message of equality forward. **In Congress, I will always fight to uphold the values Dr. King stood for.** From ensuring every vote is counted to creating pathways to opportunity for all, I am committed to building a better future for our communities.

Let’s honor Dr. King’s legacy by recommitting ourselves to this work. Together, we can be the change that Dr. King dreamed of and ensure his vision of justice and equality becomes a reality for future generations.

Onward,

Wesley

name: Wesley Bell
subject: Black history is American history
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Progress isn’t just about looking back – it’s about moving forward together. **Happy Black History Month, Peter!**

Black History Month is a time to celebrate the achievements, resilience, and contributions of Black Americans who have shaped this country – _but it’s also a time to reflect on the work that still needs to be done._

The Civil Rights Movement, the fight for racial equity, and the fight for voting rights – Black leaders have been on the frontlines. **Missouri has a proud legacy of Black leaders who have fought for justice.**

From the courtroom to the statehouse to the streets. Leaders like Homer G. Phillips, who championed Black healthcare in St. Louis. Congressman Bill Clay, who helped found the Congressional Black Caucus. And today, grassroots organizers, elected officials, and everyday Missourians are carrying that fight forward.

But let’s be clear: This work isn’t over. Across the country, extremists are trying to roll back our hard-fought progress – erasing Black history from our classrooms, suppressing our voices at the ballot box, and blocking policies that would bring real change to our communities.

More than ever, we must stay engaged. Not just in February, but every single day. That means pushing for real criminal justice reform, protecting our right to vote, expanding economic opportunity, and standing up to those who want to take us backward.

**More than ever before, we can't afford to be complacent.**

body:
Peter — _What has Donald Trump actually done for Missouri?_

The answer is: **Nothing good.**

He’s slashed funding for public schools, put unelected billionaires in charge, and gave tax breaks to the ultra-rich while leaving everyday Missourians behind.

His deep cuts to education funding will leave Missouri schools struggling, forcing teachers to do more with less, underpaying educators, and overcrowding classrooms.

And while he’s working against the best interests of working families, Trump and his allies have put billionaires and special interests in charge, prioritizing their profits over our kids, our schools, and our future.

**Missouri deserves better.** I’m fighting for fully funded public schools, an economy that works for all of us, and a government that puts people over profit.

[**Trump’s MAGA movement isn’t done screwing over everyday Missourians. I'm counting on the power of this grassroots team to help me continue fighting. We’re watching a constitutional crisis unfold in real-time — _and it’s hitting home, right here in St. Louis._

Under Donald Trump’s second term, our immigration system has become a weapon of cruelty and chaos.

International students _right here in St. Louis_ are being targeted, their visas revoked without warning, upending their lives and dreams. These are students who came here to learn, to contribute, and to build a better future. And now? **They’re caught in a political crossfire nobody asked for.**

And then there’s the case of Kilmar Abrego Garcia — _a**legal** Maryland resident, husband, and father of three children_ — who the Trump administration illegally deported to El Salvador, where he's being detained in a prison notorious for cruelty and even murder.

The Supreme Court _unanimously_ ordered his return, but the Trump administration has refused to comply. This blatant disregard for the rule of law is not just an affront to justice and due process **but to democracy itself.**

This isn’t about immigration policy. It’s about power. It’s about a president who believes he’s above the law, who uses fear and cruelty as tools of governance. It was never my intention to be a "traditional" representative, and that hasn't changed. Peter,

I want to take a minute to properly introduce myself. Not just the title or the resume, _but the person behind the ask._ Because if I’m showing up in your inbox asking for a bit of your hard-earned money, the least I can do is make sure you know who’s asking — _**and why it matters.**_

[**If you’re already familiar with who I am and why I’m fighting for St. Louis, go ahead and make a donation of $3, $5, or whatever feels right to you ahead of Wednesday’s crucial end-of-month fundraising deadline.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/106522016/541780465/552493051?refcode=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250425_eom1_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=aee79870-1c22-f011-8b3d-6045bded8cca&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYWVlNzk4NzAtMWMyMi1mMDExLThiM2QtNjA0NWJkZWQ4Y2NhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VNC0Qr0-D2HNY0I6XqxNfXHHrZCFYjtVXihYq6DOhIc=)

When I was growing up in North County, I watched my family fight for fairness on the job. My grandfather led a historic strike at a steel mill in the 60s. I didn’t fully understand what it meant when I was a kid, but I remember the pride in his voice when he talked about it.

That strike wasn’t just about wages — it was about dignity and respect and the belief that hard work should mean a better life, not just barely scraping by. Now I’m in Congress, and I carry all of that with me. For me, this job isn’t about titles; it’s about impact and doing my best to leave the world a better place than what I was born into, just like my family did. That means digging deep into criminal justice reform and public safety, showing up for working families, protecting our environment, and investing in the public health systems that keep communities strong.

**My path to Congress wasn’t a traditional one.**

My experience comes from union halls and classrooms; courtrooms and council chambers. It comes from waiting tables, running phone lines for a telephone company, teaching at the same local community college I started taking classes at when I was 17, and bouncing between odd jobs to make ends meet — and I wouldn't trade any of it.

Every job I had, and every challenge I’ve faced, led me to where I am today. And in those moments when I was working double shifts at Shoney’s or grading papers as a professor at St. Louis Community College, I knew one day I would follow in the steps of my family and have a chance to fight for the same community that raised me.

But Peter, my experience also comes from knowing when to fight like hell and when to sit down and really listen. **I promise to keep showing up as myself...not just the guy in a suit on the House floor, but the kid in a proud union family, the biggest Cardinals and Mizzou fan, a barbecue purist (sorry, Kansas City), and someone who still knows his way around a community college classroom.**

We need a little more realness in politics. And right now, I'm going to be real with you: _My team and I need your help._

We’re coming up on a crucial fundraising deadline, and these benchmarks matter — not just because the political world is always watching, but because this work takes real resources. That’s the only way we build out our organizing, amplify our message, and stay ready for whatever’s next.

clean_body: It was never my intention to be a "traditional" representative, and that hasn't changed. Peter, I want to take a minute to properly introduce myself. Not just the title or the resume, but the person behind the ask. Because if I’m showing up in your inbox asking for a bit of your hard-earned money, the least I can do is make sure you know who’s asking — and why it matters. = When I was growing up in North County, I watched my family fight for fairness on the job. My grandfather led a historic strike at a steel mill in the 60s. I didn’t fully understand what it meant when I was a kid, but I remember the pride in his voice when he talked about it. That strike wasn’t just about wages — it was about dignity and respect and the belief that hard work should mean a better life, not just barely scraping by. Now I’m in Congress, and I carry all of that with me. For me, this job isn’t about titles; it’s about impact and doing my best to leave the world a better place than what I was born into, just like my family did. That means digging deep into criminal justice reform and public safety, showing up for working families, protecting our environment, and investing in the public health systems that keep communities strong. My path to Congress wasn’t a traditional one. My experience comes from union halls and classrooms; courtrooms and council chambers. It comes from waiting tables, running phone lines for a telephone company, teaching at the same local community college I started taking classes at when I was 17, and bouncing between odd jobs to make ends meet — and I wouldn't trade any of it. Every job I had, and every challenge I’ve faced, led me to where I am today. And in those moments when I was working double shifts at Shoney’s or grading papers as a professor at St. Louis Community College, I knew one day I would follow in the steps of my family and have a chance to fight for the same community that raised me. But Peter, my experience also comes from knowing when to fight like hell and when to sit down and really listen. I promise to keep showing up as myself...not just the guy in a suit on the House floor, but the kid in a proud union family, the biggest Cardinals and Mizzou fan, a barbecue purist (sorry, Kansas City), and someone who still knows his way around a community college classroom. End of story. Peter,

It’s National Teacher Appreciation Week — **and I want to start by saying thank you to every teacher who shows up for our kids, day in and day out.**

The ones who stay late grading papers, who buy school supplies out of their own pockets, and who help shape the hearts and minds of the next generation. Missouri teachers are some of the most dedicated people I know, _and they deserve so much more than just our gratitude._

But right now, **they’re under attack.**

With Donald Trump back in the White House, his administration has made it clear: Public education is in their crosshairs.

He’s moving to dismantle the Department of Education entirely — and if that happens, Missouri schools would be some of the hardest hit.

Missouri schools would lose millions in federal support for special education, free school lunches, and programs that serve our most vulnerable students. And it doesn’t stop there...they're attacking LGBTQ+ kids, extreme groups are targeting books that challenge traditional thinking, and extreme politicians trying to dictate what can and can’t be taught in our classrooms.

Trump and his MAGA cronies are launching an all-out assault on our public schools and the people working so hard to hold them together. I’m not letting this go unanswered.

**Donald Trump can’t figure out how to lie about Medicaid cuts**

_In February, he said Medicaid “isn’t going to be touched” and then, the next day, endorsed the House bill that very much “touches” it._
Donald Trump loves to call himself an outsider.

But when it comes to gutting vital programs like Medicaid, he’s using the oldest political trick in the book.

Since his first campaign, Trump has leaned on the same tired excuse — claiming he’s just rooting out “waste, fraud, and abuse” — to distract from the real harm his budget proposals inflict on working people.

Now, he’s at it again. Trump and House Republicans are pushing a so-called “big, beautiful bill” that would extend massive tax breaks for billionaires and corporations — and to pay for it, they plan to slash at least $880 billion from Medicaid over the next decade.

**Let’s be clear: You don’t find $880 billion in “waste, fraud, and abuse.” You find it by cutting healthcare for seniors, children, working families, and people with disabilities.**

And while Trump flip-flops from saying Medicaid “won’t be touched” to endorsing the very bill that guts it, Republican leaders in Congress are scrambling to sell this betrayal with hollow promises about protecting the “most vulnerable.” If that sounds unconvincing, _it’s because it is._ Our communities deserve better than this. Healthcare is a human right — and no one should lose access to it so the ultra-wealthy can get another tax cut.

body:
Peter,

Juneteenth is more than a history lesson. It’s a celebration of resilience.

Today marks the moment in 1865 when the last enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas finally received word of their freedom, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation.

Juneteenth is a stark reminder of how far we’ve come, _and how far we still have to go in the fight for true justice and equality._ As we reflect on this day, let us honor those who endured generations of injustice and those who continue to push for a future rooted in dignity, equity, and opportunity for all.

subject: I was taught that if you’re going to do a job, you do it right.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter,

St. Louis has given me everything — it’s where I grew up, where I built my career, and where I learned what it means to fight for the community I love.

The people of this city have always had faith in me to show up when it counts, and that’s exactly what I’m doing now in Congress. More than ever before, _things are chaotic._

Too many politicians in Washington seem comfortable letting the promise of America slip through the cracks and chasing personal gain instead of public service. I was raised differently. Peter,

Last week, Republicans quickly passed Donald Trump's America-last budget bill just before the 4th of July, _and I'm livid._

This bill guts Medicaid, strips resources from our public schools, and turns its back on rural hospitals, job training programs, and everyday Missourians just trying to make ends meet. This has never been about making things better for Americans. For Trump and his allies, _**it's always been about putting themselves and their corporate enablers first.**_

But what exactly does this bill mean for Missourians? Let me explain.

First, there’s the **$900 billion in Medicaid cuts** over the next ten years, then, **$300 billion from SNAP** that will strip away food and health services from families who rely on them — just to hand another tax break to the wealthiest Americans. This will put healthcare coverage for over 150,000 of our neighbors at risk.

There’s also a provision in this big mess of a bill that slashes funding for infrastructure projects like new roads, bridges, clean water systems, and broadband expansion, which threaten the very investments rural and working communities need to grow and stay connected.

I didn’t run for Congress to sit quietly while budgets like this get forced on our communities. I ran to fight for working people, for the middle class, for the promise that if you work hard, you can build a good life right here in Missouri.

We can’t stop fighting Donald Trump’s dangerous agenda. But I can’t fight alone.

Every Missourian knows the magic of our public lands.

From the Ozark National Scenic Riverways to the trails of Wilson’s Creek National Battlefield, _these parks aren’t just places on a map_ — they’re where we fish with our families, hike with our kids, and find a little peace in the world.

RFK Jr. and Trump don't care about your health. Peter,

Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is using his power to spread dangerous misinformation about vaccines and healthcare, _and I refuse to stay quiet about it._

Earlier this year I joined my colleagues in demanding answers from RFK Jr. after he downplayed the threat of a dangerous bird flu outbreak. But instead of acting on science, he decided to double down on misinformation and conspiracy theories.

_And that's only the beginning._

Since he was handed the reins to America's public health organization, RFK Jr. has cut **$500 million** in funding for mRNA vaccine research – this is the same vaccine make-up that led us to the COVID-19 vaccine, and updated vaccines for the flu and other deadly diseases. And now, he's calling for a “review” of the recommended vaccine schedule for kids, not because of science, **but because of conspiracy theories.**

Let's be clear, Peter: This isn’t just politics, it’s plain dangerous, and it will cost people their lives. Public health experts are already underfunded and stretched thin, and pulling resources and ignoring science will make it even harder to protect our families. Every child and every family — _no matter their zip code_ — deserves access to the care, treatments, and vaccines that keep us safe.

Governor Mike Kehoe is expected to call a special session that could reopen Missouri’s congressional maps, and we know exactly who benefits if Republicans get their way: _Donald Trump and his MAGA allies._

Republicans want to follow Texas’s lead, slice up our communities, and gerrymander Missouri so Democrats barely have a fighting chance in one of eight districts.

Redistricting is supposed to happen once every decade, and it’s already been done. **But Republicans see an opportunity to twist the rules and rig the maps to their advantage so they can squeeze out more GOP seats.**

Our communities, our representation, and our democracy are not political bargaining chips for the GOP to use whenever they want. But the truth is, if they succeed, _it's Missouri voters who are going to pay the price for their reckless, self-serving games._

subject: This country is teetering on something that we can't come back from.

body:
For me, this has always been personal. I’ve spent my entire life believing in the promise of America, Peter.

Growing up in North St. Louis County, in a proud union household, I learned early that democracy only works when ordinary people are willing to stand up for one another.

My grandfather went on strike at a steel mill in 1967 so his coworkers could earn a fair wage. My stepfather wired homes as a proud member of IBEW. And when I was waiting tables at Shoney’s to pay my way through school, I carried the lessons I learned with me.

I believe that dignity comes from work, fairness comes from standing together, and justice comes only when we fight for it. But right now, what we’re seeing at the hands of one man and his extremist movement is pushing our country to a breaking point. America was never designed to function on division, fear, and self-interest, yet that’s what some would have us accept.

I’ve dedicated my career to public service, whether it was as a public defender standing beside the most vulnerable, as a Ferguson City Councilmember fighting for real police reform, or as St. Louis County Prosecutor taking on a broken system to make it more fair and accountable, I’ve seen firsthand how fragile justice and democracy can be.

Now, in Congress, I carry those lessons with me every single day, but our democracy is only as strong as we let it be. Right now, it desperately needs good people who are willing to stand up, speak out, and fight back against those who would rather see it crumble than fight for anyone but themselves. **Before we fall short of our crucial end-of-month fundraising goal for August, can I count on you to chip in to help me close the gap? >>** **[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bell-2025-q3-email&refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/114367058/566789487/554393595?ms=em25_250831_eom4_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&refcode=em25_250831_eom4_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&source=em25_250831_eom4_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_250831_eom4_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=5MPpVv8Mb0s0/NSdPeDbJJpGi2cNjQbBAtfZGB7E4R2ua4geGEek2D+4GsUGpkH/N04QQXdmHXHRr1V6R6ZOPEK/sUCYPoqH7dZ0QgMxRkgJtNXLINacSU/Ftd6f0lblkBAWcIPJUqfAzE+c/hBgZ2xlfCif+gKttpFFshJkJZA=&refcode2=9bc580e8-8b86-f011-b484-6045bdeb7413&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiOWJjNTgwZTgtOGI4Ni1mMDExLWI0ODQtNjA0NWJkZWI3NDEzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=UO0g4bXd338B1di_1lwPUoAJL-KuytPQL6rbqiSxgSA=)**

Peter,

The Missouri State Legislature has officially been called back for a special session by Governor Mike Kehoe. Not to make life better for our communities, **but to take up Donald Trump’s call to rig election maps in favor of Republicans.**

This mid-decade gerrymander is designed to lock Missouri into permanent minority rule, split apart our communities, weaken our voices, and push Black and brown Missourians out of fair representation in Congress.

_And as if that wasn’t enough,_ **Republicans are also trying to rewrite our constitution to make it nearly impossible for voters to pass ballot initiatives, an outright attack on the process Missourians have used to raise the minimum wage, defend reproductive freedom, and expand paid sick leave.**

Republicans are about one thing right now — rigging the system against Missouri voters to appease Trump, silence Kansas City, silence St. Louis, and silence you.

Cori Bush has announced she's running against Congressman Wesley Bell in the 2026 Democratic primary. Peter,

Today, Cori Bush announced she's running against Congressman Wesley Bell in the 2026 Democratic primary. No doubt in the coming months, we'll be hearing a lot of noise from her campaign.

**But, here are the facts, Peter:**

In a tenure that was plagued by scandal, incompetence, and delusion, Cori continuously put her personal agenda ahead of the needs of her constituents. She voted **against** the Child Tax Credit that would have helped 300,000 Missouri children escape poverty. She voted **no** on the infrastructure law that is creating jobs and rebuilding St. Louis' roads, bridges, and infrastructure.

Currently, Cori is under federal criminal investigation after she was caught paying her husband over $100,000 to be her bodyguard. And she's been accused of routing **hundreds of thousands of taxpayer dollars** into her own bank account.

In 2024, this district chose to go in a new direction. And we shouldn't look back.

[**The people voted Cori Bush out because she let this district down. But Wesley is focused on making life better for his constituents, and he's not done fighting for our values in Washington. If you're with him, chip in to his reelection campaign today.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/116533913/573726421/-1347839382?refcode=em25_251003_corbus_fndd_gq_act___WBFC_ettx&utm_campaign=em25_251003_corbus_fndd_gq_act___WBFC_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=e4923f7d-91a0-f011-8e61-6045bded8ba4&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTQ5MjNmN2QtOTFhMC1mMDExLThlNjEtNjA0NWJkZWQ4YmE0IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=eqUira9lvjXrg12vsGn1Y_yTxNFewqOgUHtq6zy6GRI=)

Districts like ours are under constant assault by the Trump Administration. That's why Wesley gets up every day and fights for Missouri families.
* He introduced legislation to provide compensation for St. Louis families exposed to contamination from the Manhattan Project.
* He co-sponsored a bill to invest $360 million into local gun buyback programs to make our communities safer.
* He supported legislation to keep foreign interests OUT of our democratic elections.
* And he secured nearly $7 million to increase housing supply and affordability in St. Louis.

subject: A thank you and an update:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
I have two updates, Peter.

First, thanks to your support and belief in this campaign, **we met our ambitious FEC end-of-quarter fundraising goal.** We're showing the strength of a grassroots team that's ready to keep moving St. Louis — _and our country_ — forward.

Right now, the GOP is trying to take us backward. Washington sits in a shutdown, and Americans are paying the price. 37,000 Missouri workers are facing lost pay, families risk losing WIC aid within days, and farmers and travelers could face delays. The longer this shutdown drags on, the harder it will hit Missouri communities.

But instead of working with Democrats to reopen the government, Republicans are pushing misinformation. They're claiming Democrats are asking for the sun and moon. That's flat-out false.

The truth is: Republicans are trying to rip healthcare away from _**15 million**_ hardworking Americans and raise costs for millions more. All Democrats want to do is meet at the table and secure a budget that doesn't leave working people behind.

**Republicans are doing everything they can to try and place the blame on anyone but themselves, even using government websites as platforms to spread their lies.** All this fingerpointing gets nothing done for the American people, and it fuels more partisan games while leaving communities behind.

That's why I'm so grateful to have this team. With you fighting by my side, I'm not backing down. I'll keep fighting for a budget that protects working families and puts people over politics.

From the bottom of my heart: _Thank you for your support._

— Wesley

body:
So far, Republicans are unwilling to work with us to find any real solutions. Peter,

We're now on **Day 8** of the GOP's government shutdown. Washington gridlock is hurting hardworking families who deserve better across St. Louis and the nation. But Donald Trump is twisting the knife and threatening to block furloughed federal workers from receiving back pay once the shutdown is over.

Let's be clear: Families shouldn't have to worry about missing a paycheck or losing access to services they've earned just because extreme Republicans want to play political games with people's lives.

Extreme Republicans in Congress _still_ don't have a plan to protect folks from rising health care costs or to reopen our government. **And so far, they are unwilling to work with Democrats to find any real solutions.**

But I'm staying in this fight with House Democrats to get things moving again.

Democrats will keep showing up, fighting for solutions, and standing with the people who hired us to do this job, no matter what.

This isn't strategy, it's cruelty with a side of arrogance. Peter,

Right now, hardworking Americans are going without pay while extremists in Congress hold the government hostage.

This isn't strategy, **it's cruelty with a side of arrogance.** People are living paycheck to paycheck, while Republican "leaders" are sitting in Washington twiddling their thumbs, pretending they're negotiating.

We need the government open, we need people paid for the work they've already done, and we need leaders who actually fight for their constituents.

Even when the government is shut down, the American people still need Congress to do its job. That's why I'm making sure federal disaster aid actually reaches our neighbors, calling for SNAP benefits to keep flowing, and keeping our district office open for anyone who needs help during this shutdown. Honoring our veterans means more than saying "thank you." It means showing up for them — **not just on Veterans Day, but every single day of the year.**

More than 355,000 veterans live in Missouri, and nearly 34,000 of them call Missouri's First District home. They are our friends, family members, and neighbors. They made unimaginable sacrifices to keep us safe, protect our democracy, and strengthen the rights we often take for granted.

Because of the Republican shutdown, the Department of Veterans Affairs has halted services for nearly **one million veterans.** Veterans have already given so much, and they deserve better than partisan games that threaten their care and benefits.

_Our commitment to them shouldn't end when their service does._ **That's why I've introduced bipartisan legislation that would let military retirees and all disabled veterans continue to contribute to their retirement accounts even after they separate from service.**

To every veteran in Missouri and across the country: Thank you for your service, your sacrifice, and your unwavering commitment to our nation.

With gratitude and always in solidarity,

You should have the consequences made clear to you. Peter,

Washington's dysfunction has left us with the longest government shutdown in American history.

For 43 days, Mike Johnson and Donald Trump made it clear they'd do anything to get their way. They held our healthcare, wages, and even the food on our table hostage, all while the American people paid the price.

And to top it all off, the spending bill that passed last night was just another slap in the face from GOP leadership. **The budget does nothing for the 24 million Americans who will see their healthcare costs _double_ by the end of the year.**

I have to ask, Peter: Who is Mike Johnson working for? It sure isn't Louisiana. His state is expected to see the steepest decline in healthcare coverage in the nation, a 61% drop.

This budget will have lasting consequences in Louisiana, Missouri, and across the nation. It will devastate families who are already struggling to afford their healthcare and force countless families to go without coverage.

I'm telling you this not to scare you, but because you should have the consequences made clear to you. You need to know that I voted NO on the GOP's sham deal because I believe St. Louis deserves a representative who will show up for them, not Donald Trump, not the 1%, and certainly not for themselves.

**My first priority will always be to hear and raise the voices of the people in our community. I'm in this fight for you, and I'll keep fighting to cut costs and bring our hard-earned dollars back to our district.**

In solidarity,

Spread some love this Small Business Saturday Peter,

Small Business Saturday is a reminder of what really keeps our communities going: Family-owned shops, local manufacturers, and neighborhood restaurants. It's all the people who pour their time, energy, and hearts into their businesses and communities every single day.

This Small Business Saturday, skip the big box stores and shop local! St. Louis is full of bustling neighborhoods home to businesses stocked for the holidays, from the antique stores lining Cherokee Street to the galleries and boutiques of Central West End. [SHOP ST. LOUIS](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/120218104/585600437/912318535?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNzVhOTdkN2MtM2NjZC1mMDExLTgxOTUtMDAwZDNhMWQ1OGFhIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=H7TK1tTZ280QHhN-hKkePOnn0mTBmv-BBBR4ZwnxchE=&emci=1148057b-6fc9-f011-8196-6045bdfe8e9c&emdi=75a97d7c-3ccd-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=1020964) Wesley grew up in a working-class family, and he's spent his career fighting for people who don't have an army of lobbyists behind them. In Congress, he's pushing for stable economic policies, lower costs, and fair access to capital so small businesses can hire, grow, and thrive.

But right now, **they're being pushed to the breaking point.**

Costs are up on everything from materials to groceries, and it's squeezing already-tight margins. Healthcare prices for small employers have been climbing for years, making it even harder for them to compete with big corporations. And with the GOP's reckless tariffs and high borrowing rates, too many small business owners feel like they have to "hunker down" instead of growing.

People are working harder than ever and still living paycheck to paycheck, and when families struggle, small businesses struggle too.

This Small Business Saturday, we're asking you to stand with Wesley and with every small business fighting to stay afloat. Peter,

I want to reflect on our fight for reproductive freedom in Missouri. We were the first state to ban abortion following the fall of _Roe v. Wade, _thanks to an antiquated trigger law, and last year, we were the first to end an abortion ban at the ballot box.

Despite every barrier, every scare tactic, and every desperate attempt to stop us, Missourians made our values unmistakable: We believe women should have full bodily autonomy and the ability to make the best decision for themselves and their family without government interference. The vote to restore abortion access wasn't close, and it wasn't unclear.

_But to nobody's surprise,_ **instead of respecting the will of the people, Missouri Republicans are trying to undermine our vote.** And it's not just in Missouri — radical Republicans have been chipping away at abortion access across the country.

Reproductive freedom is a winning issue. It's a right that a majority of Americans believe in. Republicans continue to be on the wrong side of history, and their actions are literally endangering the lives of millions of women across the country.

subject: Happy New Year, and a thank you

body:
St. Louis is my home, and I'm proud to represent our great city in our nation's capital and to fight for the liberties and freedoms that were promised to We The People. Happy New Year, Peter!

**2026 brings us new challenges and new opportunities, but one thing I'm certain of heading into this election year is that I'm grateful you're by my side.**

St. Louis is my home. I'm proud to represent our great city in our nation's capital and to fight to bring home the investments working families deserve.

Before we fully look forward, I want to look back at how we got to this moment. Donald Trump spent 2025 deliberately dismantling the institutions we believed to be untouchable. He's warped the presidential seat to cozy up to foreign interests, attack free speech, gut affordable healthcare access, and roll back essential environmental protections.

Prices have not gone down. In fact, they've continued to climb and squeeze working families for every penny. People are losing their health insurance coverage, Social Security is once again on the chopping block, and our nation feels more divided than ever before. If this is Trump's American Dream, _we want no part in it._

Already, the 2026 House Forecast predicts Democrats have a 62 percent chance of flipping the House blue in November. I'm determined to make that happen and to end Trump's grip on our democracy once and for all.

Thank you again for being with me in this fight, and thank you to everyone who chipped in ahead of our FEC end-of-year deadline. Reaching our goal was just the first step in many down the road to Election Day.

When we fight, we win, so let's keep pressing forward.

In solidarity,

We need to ensure as many as 51,000 Missourians can keep their health insurance. Peter,

**Wesley voted to renew the expired Affordable Care Act subsidies to ensure as many as 51,000 Missourians can keep their health insurance.[Join him in demanding the U.S. Senate acts now and renews the subsidies. Add your name to his petition.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/122988385/594101482/-501822213?ms=em26_260109_acapet_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&refcode=em26_260109_acapet_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&source=em26_260109_acapet_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260109_acapet_adv_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=MF1PnSGlWblZodG5G1EkPZQswpv2AYQ7Z5qdOdODEmJAdlHYn+/jrgoNXQU4BZQsATw96T/nKKwcqjHsIOulO2ysgvtsxZnDvN9juYA3358N4Qv+OOU5uArGkNr3toEJQ17esoJTPmAG1Zqmm2r3pGDR5IQkbE82Ajxx8HdyW7k=&refcode2=37d3b736-82ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzdkM2I3MzYtODJlZC1mMDExLTgxOTQtMDAwZDNhMTFmOTAzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=z9BIQPczXfjBuFmeZ0Gy_FKofIYUrEppjNobdcKEsEM=&emci=1f23b108-b1ec-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=37d3b736-82ed-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=1020964)**

The Affordable Care Act works because it makes coverage affordable. But the tax credits that keep premiums low just expired, and thanks to the GOP's floundering, costs are going to go up, _a lot._

For many working families right here in Missouri, this won't be survivable. It will mean parents dropping coverage, seniors skipping care, and countless young Americans going uninsured and hoping nothing goes wrong.

We've seen this before, Peter.

**When healthcare gets too expensive, people don't stop getting sick; they just stop getting help.**

The ACA helped cut uninsured rates across the country and protected people from crushing medical debt. Letting these credits expire undoes years of progress in one stroke. body:
Congress needs to remember who it answers to: YOU. Hey Peter, At midnight tonight, we'll hit our first fundraising deadline of the election year.

But before I take one last moment to tell you why I'm running to represent Missouri in Congress, I have to ask: [**Will you chip in $5, or anything you can, to help me build a winning campaign and flip the House blue?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123408184/595386495/-250409404?refcode=em26_260115_mm3_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260115_mm3_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=a4e8bcae-76f2-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYTRlOGJjYWUtNzZmMi1mMDExLTgxOTQtMDAwZDNhMTFmOTAzIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=yeZu46_yhlpqBnJ-AhZCDYcpDsrlUByz4oauC0DJgd4=)

Right now, too many politicians have forgotten who they work for. Too many are more interested in headlines than in helping the people who sent them to Washington.

I've always believed in public service, and that if you make a commitment to fight for real people, then you show up and do the job... _and you do it well._ But public service has always been personal for me.

My dad spent 25 years as a police officer, and growing up, my family taught me that when you have the opportunity to make a difference, you take it, even when it seems impossible. In Ferguson, Missouri, that meant trying to help calm tensions between police and protesters. In 2018, it meant taking on a seven-term incumbent and winning, because the status quo wasn't good enough for St. Louis.

Today, it means listening to my community and stepping up again, not for attention or for personal or political ambition, but to serve and to fight back when our rights and voices are actively being cast aside by a small majority of extremists. Public service is in my DNA, and that means being willing to take on tough fights. Simply put: I'm really not interested in being part of the noise in Washington.

subject: Discomfort isn't a flaw, it's the point Dr. King was trying to make.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter,

Today is Martin Luther King Jr. Day, a reminder to us all that the pursuit of justice was _never meant to be comfortable._

We're seeing this in real time as thousands of brave Americans take to the streets in Minneapolis, Chicago, New York City, _and St. Louis_ to protest ICE and Donald Trump's tyranny.

Like the activists today, Dr. King understood real change would be disruptive. Throughout his lifetime, he and other Civil Rights activists fearlessly made "good trouble" in the pursuit of true justice.

In his famous _Letter from Birmingham Jail,_ Dr. King warned us of a person who is "more devoted to order than to justice...who constantly says, 'I agree with you in the goal you seek, but I can't agree with your methods of direct action...'" Right now, when the future of our democracy is on the line and the rights of fellow Americans hang in the balance, it is beyond frustrating to hear support in theory but hesitation in practice.

Dr. King's words haven't aged a day — _justice still makes people uncomfortable._ **But here's the real kicker, Peter: discomfort isn't a flaw. It's the point Dr. King was trying to make.**

In Congress, I will always fight to uphold the values Dr. King stood for, not just in words but in practice. From ensuring every vote is counted to creating pathways to opportunity for all, I am committed to building a better future for our communities.

On this MLK Day, the best way we can honor Dr. King is by living his true legacy. In the face of grave injustice, let us do the hard thing, the right thing, and keep speaking up and speaking out.

In solidarity,

Wesley

subject: Politicians shouldn't be able to make decisions about your body…but they're still trying.

body:
This is my promise to you all: Peter,

Today marks another anniversary of the original _Roe v. Wade_ decision — a reminder of what this country once recognized as a basic truth: **women deserve the freedom to make decisions about their own bodies, their own families, and dictate their own futures.**

But thanks to a small minority of anti-choice extremists, that freedom was ripped away in 2022 by the Supreme Court — leaving it up to each state to decide its own protection for abortion rights. In 2024, Missouri voters spoke up and voted to enshrine the right to an abortion in our state constitution. But just like with _Roe,_ Republicans across our state are determined to undo the will of the people.

Missouri's 2024 amendment gave us hope and said loud and clear that Americans deserve the right to make their own choices about their bodies without politicians looking over their shoulders. **Yet Republican lawmakers are pushing a confusing ballot measure that twists the truth, claiming it's about "exceptions" while really aiming to take away fundamental rights.**

This fight isn't just limited to Missouri — all across the country, states are using ballot measures to expand rights in some places and restrict them in others. But I want to be crystal clear about something, Peter: banning abortion doesn't stop abortion; it stops safe abortion. It forces people to travel, to wait, to put their health at risk, and it punishes the doctors who are just trying to do their jobs, _even in states with protections._

Courts, legislators, and politicians keep finding ways to chip away at access, rewrite the rules, and try to confuse voters. This anniversary isn't about celebrating a court decision made in 1973; it's about remembering the people who've been hurt, the providers silenced, and the generations who deserve better than lawmakers making decisions for them. Reproductive care IS healthcare, and no politician or judge should get to touch the choices you make about your own body. **End of story.**

subject: Honoring the past, facing the truth.

body:
Happy Black History Month! **Happy Black History Month, Peter!**

Black History Month is about more than honoring the past. It's about telling the truth about where we've been, what we've survived, and what's being asked of us right now.

Black Americans have always been on the frontlines of building this country and pushing it to live up to its promise. From the courthouse to the Capitol, from the pulpit to the picket line, Black leaders and Black communities have led the fight for justice, dignity, and equal protection under the law.

Missouri's history is filled with that leadership...and so is its present. But right now, we need to be honest with ourselves, Peter. Across the country, we are seeing renewed racial targeting and intimidation. Families are living in fear, communities are being singled out, and enforcement systems are being used in ways that echo some of the darkest chapters of our history.

When immigration enforcement is weaponized through racial profiling, and when people are targeted because of how they look or where they come from, it undermines the very idea of justice. This administration is sending us a message that it believes our rights to be expendable. But Black History Month reminds us that our ancestors **never** asked for permission before demanding our rights be recognized and our voices heard.

Groceries cost more.

Gas costs more.

Rent and utilities keep going up.

And the job market isn't what it needs to be for folks to keep up.

For too many Missourians, it feels like they're doing everything right — working hard, playing by the rules — and still falling further behind.**That's not right, and it's not what opportunity is supposed to look like,_especially not in the wealthiest nation on earth_. **

❌ Jacking up prices with illegal tariffs, then giving a $175 billion bailout to the same corporations passing costs on to us.

🗳️ I’m fighting back against MAGA attempts to overturn our elections.
