subject: Political theater won't deliver justice to survivors
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Republicans know exactly what they're doing. Peter,

As a former prosecutor, I've led these kinds of depositions before, and I know what a serious investigation looks like. What we're seeing right now in the Epstein investigation is straight up political theater.

And that's not just frustrating — it's dangerous and borderline evil. Did Republicans forget that there are real victims and survivors, or do they just not care? Epstein's survivors deserve justice, which means a full, transparent investigation that follows the evidence, **_wherever it goes._**

Instead, what we're getting is selective outrage.

If you want to depose the Clintons? _Fine._

If you want to hear from President Trump? _Fine._

The first lady? Elon Musk? Anyone with relevant information? _Fine._

**Republican or Democrat, I really don't care what letter is in front of your name.**

You don't get to subpoena _just_ Democrats for headlines and then suddenly lose interest when it comes to Republicans. You don't get to close the doors to the public, deny transparency, and then leak photos for clicks.

That's not oversight, that's a show. And survivors deserve better than a show. There are still missing Epstein files and unanswered questions. body:
Peter,

When I think about the women who shaped my life, **I think about my mom.** Growing up, I watched her build a strong career in public service, helping people while also holding our family together, facing every challenge along the way with strength and more grace than I probably deserved (raising me was not always the easiest assignment). Her example inspired me to run for office and dedicate my life to serving others. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/126913904/606356712/-454253735?ms=em26_260308_intwms_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&refcode=em26_260308_intwms_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&source=em26_260308_intwms_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260308_intwms_fndd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&contactdata=PUUBlkrGlwjTlYcsBHTM0EeaxsdaZA5XlKlNAgi4N7nHKO6/0slgS2n7y7d2Su8tEu+d8C6tWbyorniwtqN1jRiYRv57AfEBD2DFYaXyNepzC8lZ7M3SrfloZoNnP6nfcNFHEqtB0rgcLdz5Qu/i2QA7BENbWWigeRqUWMjmf5M=&refcode2=c479bbad-031b-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYzQ3OWJiYWQtMDMxYi1mMTExLWE2OWEtMDAwZDNhMWYwYTk3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AtqUj067J8p0_FpkQ5WKEIr2xC1mEjhKoJHW7CGGfdU=&emci=fd7c51e3-8919-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&emdi=c479bbad-031b-f111-a69a-000d3a1f0a97&ceid=1020964) That’s part of why it makes me so angry to see what’s happening right now. Republicans will tell you they’re not attacking women’s rights. _But while they play dumb, the reality looks very different._

We see it in the endless crusade to strip away women’s bodily autonomy through abortion bans and attacks on funding for critical health care programs. We see it in the _SAVE Act,_ which could make voting harder for millions of married women. And there are even groups openly advocating for “single household voting,” where essentially only the man in a married household would get a vote.

This is a bold-faced attempt to drag this country backward. I’ve always believed our society is stronger when everyone has a voice. **_Frankie Muse Freeman. Maya Angelou. Ora Lee Malone. Josephine Baker._**

Peter, what do these women all have in common? **If you guessed they all share roots in St. Louis, you'd be right!**

**Frankie Muse Freeman** served as an Assistant Attorney General for her state and later became the first woman appointed to the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights.

**Maya Angelou** , the beloved poet, author, and activist, told the world why the caged bird sings. She worked alongside Martin Luther King Jr. and Malcolm X and used her words to inspire generations.

**Ora Lee Malone** , a trailblazer in the labor movement, organized a garment factory union made up largely of Black workers. Today, she's recognized as one of the first leaders to connect the fight for racial and gender equality with the broader movement for working-class economic justice.

**Josephine Baker** , an international icon of music and dance, used her fame to fight segregation. She was the only official female speaker at the 1963 March on Washington and refused to perform for segregated audiences, even protesting discriminatory venues like the New York Stork Club.

This Women's History Month, we're celebrating the incredible Black women who helped shape our city's story and pushed our country forward.

At a time when the Trump administration is working overtime to erase the contributions of Black women across the country, Wesley is proud to stand up for the truth. In Congress, he has pushed back against attacks on voting rights that disproportionately affect Black communities and spoken out to defend Black history museums and institutions. But protecting and honoring the legacy of Black women is a responsibility that belongs to all of us.

body:
Peter,

Our first end-of-quarter fundraising deadline of the year is coming up.

And what gets reported at the end of this quarter won't just sit in a filing cabinet— _it will be public for everyone (including our opponents and deep-pocketed Republicans) to see._

It will shape how this campaign is seen, how much momentum we have, and whether or not we're positioned to reelect Wesley to represent our district this November.

At the same time, the work hasn't slowed down, **not even for a second.** Wesley has been focused on delivering real results for St. Louisans—not headlines, not talking points, but tangible investments in the community. That means:
* **$3.1 million secured to modernize power infrastructure at St. Louis Lambert International Airport**

* **$1 million delivered to Ferguson to revitalize the Farmers Market and create a permanent, accessible community space**

* **Support for a bipartisan effort to expand Gateway Arch National Park into East St. Louis**

* **Introduction of the _EPSTEIN Act_ to push for transparency and accountability at the federal level**

This is what it looks like to stay focused on what matters: investing in infrastructure, looking out for our community, and fighting for accountability. _It's also exactly why reelecting Wesley in November is so important._

But reaching our critical end-of-quarter fundraising goal is going to take resources—and how this team chooses to show up in moments like this one can shape the entire trajectory of this election.

A strong end-of-quarter report sends a clear message that this campaign has momentum, and we have what it takes to win. body:
Peter,

I am honored to have earned the endorsement of Planned Parenthood Action Fund—and I'm especially proud to be the **only** candidate in this race with their support.

This isn't just another endorsement.

**It's recognition of who has _actually_ been in the fight and who will keep fighting when it counts most.** Look, I have always believed that everyone deserves the freedom to make their own healthcare decisions without politicians getting in the way.

That shouldn't be controversial. Yet, **Republicans in Washington have gone out of their way to make women's access to basic healthcare a dangerous political bargaining chip.**

When extremists overturned _Roe v. Wade,_ I didn't wait to act. I joined more than 80 prosecutors across the country in making one thing clear: I would not prosecute anyone for seeking or providing an abortion. No one should ever be criminalized for a personal, often lifesaving, healthcare decision.

Some people talk about protecting rights. _Others step up when it actually matters._

And the truth is...we're still in the middle of this fight. In Missouri, the Republican supermajority is working overtime to override the will of the people. Missourians JUST voted to enshrine abortion rights in 2024—and already, anti-abortion extremists are trying to undo it and drag us backward.

I'm going to keep doing everything I can to protect and expand reproductive freedoms alongside Planned Parenthood Action Fund in Missouri and all over the country. But I can't do it alone.

Just competency. That's it. Peter,

**A lot of people are frustrated right now.**

I can feel it in my conversations with friends, at work, at home—there's a real sense that things aren't moving in the right direction, and people are tired of it.

And people aren't asking for anything over the top. They're simply asking for leaders who take their jobs seriously by staying focused and remembering who they're supposed to be working for.

That frustration is valid. _But it can't be the end of the story._

Because the only way things actually get better is if we decide to push forward anyway to build something better, more fair, and more stable than what we're seeing right now. **But that simply won't happen on its own.**

It takes people showing up, paying attention, and doing what they can, where they can, to move things in the right direction. This is what governing looks like...when you don't know how to do it 😬 Peter,

Congressional Republicans are breaking records...but for all the wrong reasons.

The GOP-led House is paralyzed, leaving critical departments shut down, bills stalled, and hardworking Americans left holding the bag.

Under Speaker Mike Johnson, **this Congress has set a record for the fewest roll-call votes in decades, blocked amendments to legislation at historic levels, and avoided votes on bills that actually have majority support.**

In short: _they're not governing—they're stalling, posturing, and letting dysfunction run wild._

Meanwhile, essential programs and agencies like the Department of Homeland Security are stuck in a shutdown, while Republicans cling to procedural games instead of solving real problems. Every single day, their lack of leadership costs families, workers, and communities across the country their financial freedom, their livelihoods, their basic rights, and so much more.

**This can't continue.** We need leadership that actually works on behalf of the American people, that fights for the common good and not for themselves, and that refuses to let dysfunction dictate our nation's future. But momentum matters, and it's on all of us to ensure that when our FEC fundraising numbers go public for the first time this year, we have a strong showing of support behind us.

body:
_The political tides are shifting, Peter._

Across the country, Democrats are winning in places experts and opponents wrote off as safe for Republicans.

We're seeing real momentum building in key House races, and local elections in deep-red states that were once written off are suddenly becoming competitive—**and very much in play.** That didn't happen by accident — it's the result of organizing, persistence, and people who refused to accept that change was impossible.

And it means something bigger is now within reach: A real path to taking back the House and putting a check on this administration's extreme, reckless, straight-up dangerous agenda. But Peter, the thing about momentum is that it really only matters if it's sustained.

Every cycle has a moment where energy starts to build, and then the question becomes whether or not it can actually be carried all the way through November. body:
Peter,

What we're watching right now across our government is a mess.

The Trump administration is treating governance like a punchline. The GOP is making never-ending chaotic decisions, pushing deeply unserious priorities, and a steady stream of headlines that would be unbelievable if they weren't happening in real time.

And while the noise gets louder, working people are the ones paying the price. Costs are up, stability feels shaky, trust in our democracy is being chipped away day by day, and unless you're one of Trump's well-connected, deep-pocketed buddies, it's getting harder to feel like the system is even built for you anymore. And that's not normal.

I'm not here to be polite about it and pretend that what we're seeing is even remotely okay, on any level. Restoring accountability and basic decency to our government starts with taking back control of the House and protecting seats like this one.

This campaign will ALWAYS champion the fight for an America that works for everyone, not just the powerful few at the top. Every dollar right now directly fuels voter outreach, organizing, and the work it takes to win tough races across the country. House Republicans just hauled in **$47 million** in a record-breaking fundraising push ahead of November's midterm elections, and it's clear why:

_They're desperate to cling to their fading majority in Congress._

They know their grip on the House is hanging by a thread, and with so much of their power on the line, they're scrambling to post massive fundraising numbers as early as possible to tout their campaign warchest.

Peter, the GOP is showing us exactly what happens when you have almost nothing real to run on, and the strategy becomes painfully obvious — raise as much money as you can and try to buy your way into power. body:
Peter,

I want to say thank you for helping us close out April on solid footing.

We had an important end-of-month fundraising deadline ahead of us, and the fact that we met it comes down to people like you stepping up when it mattered.

And I've never taken that for granted.

**Your support gives this team room to plan ahead instead of scrambling, and it keeps us focused on the work itself.** Contributions of any amount— _especially at the end of the month, and especially during an election year_ —from people who believe in this work and this campaign are what keep us moving at a steady pace.

body:
I refuse to sit idly by and watch voters in our district be blatantly silenced. Peter,

Just last week, the Supreme Court issued a ruling that weakens parts of _The Voting Rights Act, _**and it could have real consequences here in St. Louis.**

The SCOTUS decision opens a window for state lawmakers to redraw congressional maps — _and there's a real risk Missouri Republicans will try to gerrymander MO-01 as early as this year._

This didn't happen overnight. Republicans have been chipping away at _The Voting Rights Act_ for decades. This latest ruling further weakens the guardrails that were supposed to protect communities of color from being divided up for political gain. The rules are even looser now, and Missouri Republicans have more room to move quickly when it comes to redistricting.

A lot of the recent map fights in Missouri have been playing out in Kansas City and the courts. But now the pressure is shifting, and St. Louis is directly in the spotlight. **When maps get redrawn like this, it's not just lines on paper. It changes whose voices get heard, and it changes who has power.**

The people of St. Louis — _especially Black voters_ — have spent decades building representation in this district. That work is now at risk of being undone.

Even if nothing changes before this election, the door is now open for future attempts to reshape the district in a way that weakens voter power. That's why I'm not waiting to see what happens next. We're organizing, fighting back, and making sure people understand what's at stake.

Growing up, I thought there was genuinely nothing that she couldn’t do. She was a dedicated public servant who somehow still managed to hold our family together. _She made sure we were taken care of, kept us grounded, and somehow always knew exactly when I was about to do or say something stupid._

Looking back now, I can admit she gave me a whole lot more grace than I probably deserved.

It was like watching Superwoman in action right before my eyes. The older I get, the more I realize just how many Superwoman moms are out there today.

A lot of them are doing all of that while the cost of living keeps climbing, childcare gets more expensive, public schools are under attack, and basic stability feels harder and harder to hold onto. **And yet, they still show up to save the day.**

Today, I’m thinking about my mom and every mother doing everything she can to help her family thrive. To all of you out there, I'm working in Congress to make your life a little easier and give you the breathing room you more than deserve. Even under the Trump administration, know you have an ally in D.C.

Happy Mother’s Day to the women who keep families, communities, and this country moving forward every single day.

body:
I refuse to move on until St. Louis gets the help and resources we deserve. Peter, a year ago, countless lives changed in a matter of minutes.

The tornadoes that tore through St. Louis and communities across Missouri left behind devastation that many families are still living with today.

In North St. Louis— _especially in historically Black neighborhoods that are already too often overlooked_ —homes were damaged, power was lost, streets were torn apart, and infrastructure that had been neglected for years **got even worse.**

At a time when communities like ours still need help rebuilding, **we're seeing critical support gutted instead of strengthened.** A year later, too many people are still hurting. Folks in North St. Louis are still living with the aftermath of this storm, and too many leaders have failed to move with the urgency families deserve.

St. Louis families are facing damaged homes, insurance battles, unsafe conditions, and the emotional weight of trying to put their lives back together while feeling like government leaders have moved on. **But I want you to know this: I will keep fighting for you until addressing this devastation is met with the urgency it has always deserved.**

Since day one, my team and I have been working to bring resources back home and fight for the support our communities deserve. We've pushed for federal help, worked with local partners, and kept pressing for the kind of investment that should never have been optional in the first place. I will keep fighting to restore our neighborhoods and rebuild our communities so they are safer and stronger than ever before.

Thank you,

Wesley

_That's good news._

For a lot of people, medication abortion is the only way they're able to access the care they need. But the fact is, this case is still moving through the courts. And the people trying to make abortion harder to access have not stopped, and won't until they get their way.

All we've seen since _Roe_ was overturned is extremist politicians and judges trying to take more and more control over deeply personal healthcare decisions. And the people trying to make abortion harder to access have not stopped, and won't until they get their way. subject: May has been busy, but in a good way.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
I wouldn't trade this job for anything, Peter. Peter—May has been busy, _but in a good way._

I've spent this month meeting with St. Louisans, talking to the good people who make our community strong, and doing the work you elected me to do.

I heard directly from folks during our telephone town hall about what's weighing on them right now, from rising costs, healthcare, and defending our rights to whether Washington is _actually_ paying attention to the affordability crisis our families are facing every day.

I've been fighting to bring real resources home, including securing $30 million in federal funding for Lambert Airport's new terminal project and introducing the _Tornado Preparedness Act_ after the devastating storm that changed the lives of St. Louis families last year.

Along the way, I stood alongside neighbors speaking up for voting rights and was honored to earn the endorsement of Teamsters Local 682—support that means a lot to me as a former union member.

When I ran for Congress, I promised I'd stay connected to this community and fight for working people. And I'm proud to say that that's what this month, _and this entire campaign,_ have been about.

And it's also why taking back our Democratic majority in the House is a MUST. We need leaders willing to protect our rights, invest in our communities, and make government work for everyday people again, not just the wealthy and well-connected. body:
Peter, a lot of people are overwhelmed right now, and I can't blame them.

Under Republican "leadership," we've watched abuse of power become routine and democratic norms treated like they're optional. And for a lot of families, _the consequences feel deeply personal:_

**Communities are being targeted by aggressive ICE raids that leave families living in fear.

Women are waking up every day wondering what rights Republicans will try to take away next.

Working families are stretching every dollar at the grocery store, struggling to keep up as costs keep rising.

People are rationing life-saving medication because they simply can't afford what they need.

At the same time, Republicans in Washington are gutting critical programs people rely on while pouring money into political vanity projects.**

_And that's not even the half of it, Peter._

body:
Peter,

Today, we celebrate Juneteenth — a day that marks the end of slavery in the United States and honors the resilience, strength, and contributions of Black Americans throughout our nation's history.

**Juneteenth is a reminder that progress doesn't happen on its own.**

Every generation has been called to continue the work of building a country that lives up to its promises of freedom, equality, and opportunity for all. As we reflect on this important day, we must also recognize that the fight for justice is ongoing.

We owe it to those who came before us — and those who will come after us — to keep working toward a future where every person is treated with dignity and respect. Today is a time to celebrate Black history, Black culture, and the countless individuals who have helped move our country forward, often in the face of tremendous obstacles.

Wishing you a meaningful Juneteenth.

_Tired of the division.

Tired of the dysfunction.

Tired of watching politicians focus on everything except the challenges families are facing every day._

**And I can't blame them for feeling this way.**

But I also believe that when people come together around a shared purpose, we can still make real progress. That's why I'm running for reelection in the first place, and it's why this campaign matters so much to me.

With our Democratic primary just around the corner on August 4, the work we're doing now will have a real impact on what comes next. Every voter we reach, every conversation we have, and every volunteer we get helps us organize and build the kind of campaign it takes to win.

Peter, at the end of this month, we'll publicly report our fundraising numbers. Those numbers will be scrutinized by everyone from political observers to our opponents, who use them to gauge the strength of campaigns like ours and decide where to invest their resources. body:
[IMAGE LOADING...] Peter,

When voters head to the ballot box on August 4th, they deserve to know _exactly_ what choice they're making. This race isn't about who has the loudest voice — **it's about who has delivered for St. Louis.**

And the contrast is clear: [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135149604/633264202/114933226?refcode=em26_260712_MM1_fnd_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260712_MM1_fnd_gq_act___TB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=e99a14b0-1f7e-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZTk5YTE0YjAtMWY3ZS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=YinGWDUYm2jvo1RhjtFlGFtqRawNksS9sbe3WVjS_yw=) While Wesley has focused on fighting for our communities, bringing investments home, and working to improve the lives of Missouri families, Cori Bush has repeatedly put politics ahead of results.

**We're proud of Wesley's record because it isn't built on empty promises — it's built on showing up, doing the work, and delivering for the people he represents.** Now we have to make sure every voter across St. Louis sees that difference.

August 4th is make or break for this campaign. Peter, earlier this month, we celebrated our nation's 250th birthday.

Milestones like this are a chance to reflect not only on our history, **but also on the responsibility each generation has to protect the democracy we've inherited.**

_That responsibility feels especially urgent right now._

Donald Trump and his circus of Republican yes-men in Congress are attacking the very institutions that have kept our democracy strong for all these years. They're undermining the rule of law, sowing distrust in our elections, and trying to drag our country backward.

_And they're doing it all without an ounce of shame._

I want to be as clear as I possibly can here, Peter: Celebrating this country — _and truly having love for it_ — means fighting for it. It means standing up for our democracy, protecting our freedoms, and making sure **every person** has a voice in the future we build together.

Look: the reason I decided to run for Congress in the first place is because I believe in the promise of this country. I believe the American Dream should still be within reach for every family willing to work hard. I believe our democracy is worth protecting. And I believe that when we come together, there isn't a challenge we can't overcome.

Peter, democracy only works when people participate. And in just **three days** , voters will head to the polls to make their voice heard in our Primary Election.

But before voting officially begins, we want to know: _are you prepared?_

If you haven't already, now is the time to make your plan to vote. Take a few minutes to go through our voter checklist to make sure you've covered all the basics — from confirming your registration and polling location to checking your voting options and knowing what to bring on Election Day.
**Voter Checklist:**

☐**Confirm you're registered to vote.** Make sure your registration is active and your information is up to date.

☐******Know your voting plan.** Decide whether you'll vote early, by mail (if available), or on Election Day.

☐ **Find your polling place.** Don't wait until the last minute — know exactly where you'll vote.

☐ **Check what ID you need.** Review your state's voter ID requirements before heading to the polls.

☐**Mark Election Day on your calendar.** Set a reminder so you don't forget.

☐ **Bring a friend or family member.** Voting together helps strengthen turnout.
A few minutes of preparation now can make all the difference when it's time to cast your ballot.

body:
Peter,

Because of this team, because of your belief, your time, your conversations with neighbors, your donations, your phone calls, your knocks on doors, and your faith in what we're building together, **we won our primary.**

From the bottom of my heart: _thank you_.

This campaign has never been about one person. It's been about people who believe our communities deserve leaders who will show up, listen, and fight for them every single day.

Whether you volunteered, chipped in, talked to your friends and family, or simply believed in this campaign from the very beginning, _you made this victory possible._ I'm incredibly grateful for the trust you've placed in me, and I truly don't take it lightly. But while today is a moment to celebrate, _it's also the beginning of our next challenge._ **The path to the general election starts right now, Peter.**

The campaign we've built is strong, but we'll need every bit of that energy to carry us through November. Today, I hope you'll take a moment to celebrate what we've accomplished together, you've earned it. Then, when you're ready, I hope you'll stay in this fight with me. Together, we'll keep building the campaign we need to win in November and continue fighting for the people of St. Louis. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for believing in this campaign.

**Now, let's finish what we started.**

With gratitude,

Wesley

Peter,

**We won our primary — and we couldn't have done it without you.** _But that wasn't the finish line._

subject: I have never forgotten my roots, Peter.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
Peter,

Growing up in St. Louis as the son of a police officer and county civil servant, I learned early on what it meant to work hard and look out for the people around you.

I went to Hazelwood East, worked multiple jobs to put myself through college, and eventually came home to serve this community. St. Louis made me who I am, **and every single day I'm in Congress, I remember exactly who sent me there and who I'm fighting for.**

I'm fighting for families watching their grocery bills climb, seniors worried about the cost of their prescriptions, and workers who deserve good-paying jobs and a fair shot — all while standing up to a Trump administration and MAGA Republicans threatening our rights, our democracy, and the communities we're supposed to serve.

I've learned that real change doesn't happen by sitting on the sidelines; it happens when people show up, do the work, and keep going. Peter, we won our primary earlier this month because people across St. Louis — _people like you_ — came together and put their faith in this campaign, and I'm incredibly grateful for that trust, **but our work isn't finished.**

Now, we have to carry that momentum through November and ensure this campaign has what it takes to cross the general election finish line. **That's why I'm reaching out personally, asking you to chip in anything you can before midnight tonight to help my campaign hit our mid-month fundraising goal and keep me fighting for St. Louis in Congress. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bell-q3-2026?refcode2=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137267122/640224354/114933226?refcode=em26_260815_MM3_fnd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260815_MM3_fnd_gq_act___WB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=0b629d37-a998-f111-9b33-000d3a11fa30&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDYzODkiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGI2MjlkMzctYTk5OC1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAwZDNhMTFmYTMwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JXFAHsyf2HSnDdWZ8EhJv_mCZlgvu45MNrmb4LULrbo=)**

subject: Something I still believe.

body:
64 days out, Peter. Peter,

I've spent most of my life here in St. Louis.

I grew up in North County, the son of a police officer and a county civil servant. I worked multiple jobs to put myself through college, went to law school, and came home to become a public defender.

Years later, when protests erupted just blocks from my home in Ferguson, I showed up. I stood with my neighbors, and in the years that followed, I worked to reform systems that had lost the trust of too many people in our community. None of that was part of some grand plan to end up in Congress.

_**I did it because this is my home, these are my neighbors, and this is the place I love.**_

But I've always believed that when you have the opportunity to make things better, you have a responsibility to try. That belief has taken me from the courtroom, to the Ferguson City Council, to the St. Louis County Prosecutor's Office, and _now to Congress._

It's been the honor of a lifetime getting to represent St. Louis in the House. Now, just **64 days out from Election Day,** and at midnight tonight, we close the books on a critical end-of-month fundraising deadline for August, and right now, we're still short of our goal.

subject: Donald Trump wants to make voting harder
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY BELL FOR MISSOURI
body:
It's never going to stop, not unless we end it at the ballot box. Peter,

Voting should be simple: If you're eligible to vote, you should be able to make your voice heard. _Period._ But right now, **that fundamental right is under attack.**

Donald Trump and his allies are targeting mail-in voting, and now, battles over how Americans cast their ballots are reaching the Supreme Court.

These attacks aren't just about changing election rules, Peter. They're about making it harder for people to participate in our democracy and have a say in the decisions that shape their lives.

**Our democracy is strongest when every American can exercise their fundamental right to vote.** Wesley has always fought to protect that right and ensure that the voices of everyday people are heard — and he isn't about to stop now.

subject: Trump wants his name on the USS Doris Miller?

body:
Trump wants to erase Black history Doris Miller was a hero, Peter.

During the attack on Pearl Harbor, Miller — a Black sailor serving in a segregated Navy — stepped beyond the limits of his rank to help wounded sailors and defend his ship.

His courage saved lives and earned him a place in American history. **That's why the Navy named the USS Doris Miller in his honor.** Now, President Trump is considering renaming the ship, _**erasing a powerful tribute to a Black American hero.**_

We don't know what the Navy would rename the carrier yet, but according to reports, **there's been talk of naming it after Trump himself.** That's never been done for a sitting president. clean_body: Trump wants to erase Black history Doris Miller was a hero, Peter. During the attack on Pearl Harbor, Miller — a Black sailor serving in a segregated Navy — stepped beyond the limits of his rank to help wounded sailors and defend his ship. Now, President Trump is considering renaming the ship, erasing a powerful tribute to a Black American hero. Peter, I know your inbox is probably full of political emails. Mine is too.

So when you see one come through with my name on it, I wouldn't blame you for thinking, _did Wesley actually write this?_

So let me be the first to tell you: _Yes. I actually wrote this email._

I wanted to reach out myself because we have an important end-of-quarter deadline coming up at the end of this month — and instead of waiting until the final few days to send you a bunch of increasingly frantic emails, I'm hoping we can get ahead of it together.

Here's why this one matters so much to me, and why it should matter this much to all of us:

**The numbers we report at the end of this quarter are going to be made public.** Republicans will see them. Political insiders will see them. And they'll use those numbers to make assumptions about the strength of this team and our ability to compete in the fights ahead.

And Peter, I want them to see something unmistakable: **We're here, we're strong, and we have what it takes to take back the House.**

That's why I'm asking you personally today. Peter, I wanted to send you one last note before tonight's midnight fundraising deadline.

It's not lost on me that, in just a few weeks, voters across St. Louis will decide who they want fighting for them in Congress.

Look, I grew up here. St. Louis made me who I am. And every single day I get to represent this community in Congress is an honor I'll never take for granted. We've accomplished a lot together, _but I know there is so much more work ahead of us._

I want to keep fighting to lower costs for working families.

To protect access to healthcare.

To bring federal resources and good-paying jobs home to St. Louis.

And to make sure the people I represent always have someone in Washington willing to stand up for them.

But first, **we have to make it through November.**

Tonight at midnight will mark the start of our final end-of-quarter fundraising deadline before Election Day, and I'm hoping you'll help make sure we enter these last few weeks with everything we need to bring this thing home.
